title: queue burn-rate checklist
content:
Morning micro-checklist for queue burn-rate / capacity on west/gpool clusters. Personal scratchnotes — run these, update Slack, escalate if > 30% deviation from expected burn.

Context:
- Last 12h token throughput drifted up ~28% on gpool-west-1 (nv48 profiles). Peak tail latency still within SLO but unit burn increased. Suspect batching config + a few heavy chat sessions (customer sandbox).
- Today: 6h planned spike (load test) from solutions-eng at 11:00 PST — coordinate.

Quick metrics snapshot (run from grafana shortcuts):
- command: open grafana -> dashboard "gpool-west-1 / queue-burn" -> timeframe 1h
- quick numbers to paste in Slack: tokens/min = 1.2M (baseline 950k), active-infers = 420 (baseline 360), avg-latency = 82ms

Immediate checklist (do in order):
1) Check dominant model routes:
   - curl to router: GET /routes?region=west&pool=gpool-west-1
   - note any route with > 60% traffic
2) Verify batching window settings for heavy routes:
   - check rollout flags: flags/batching/window-ms
   - if window > 12ms and latency comfortable, nudge down to 8ms for burst smoothing
3) Inspect KV cache hit rate (cause of token burn if low):
   - grafana panel "kv-cache-hit-rate"
   - threshold: if < 68% for > 10m, open quick incident note
4) Spot OLAP queries from solutions-eng (they use longer sequences):
   - grep logs: production-requests | sequence_length > 1024
   - DM @jordan for session IDs to cross-check
5) Autoscale / capacity check:
   - kubectl get hpa -n inference
   - check gpool nodes: gcloud compute instances list --filter="name:gpool-west*"
   - if spare GPUs < 2 and projected burst > 10%, consider scale-up request (ping infra on-call)
6) Rolling fallback plan (if burn continues):
   - switch heavy routes to quantized-compat model variant (q4_0) via router config (canary) — small perf impact but lowers tokens/unit cost

Who to ping and when:
- If tokens/min > 1.5M for 15m -> hit #infra-ops and @aisha
- For node preemption events / GPU loss -> escalate to SRE on-call via PagerDuty

Notes to self (todo items to turn into tickets):
- Create a workload profile for solutions-eng sandbox sessions (label: se-sandbox) — include sample prompts, avg seq len, model family
- Add grafana alert: kv-cache-hit-rate < 65% for 10m -> create incident
- Add runbook snippet for quick quantized shift (safe rollback steps)

Commands I used / snippets to save:
- kubectl logs deployment/router -n inference --since=15m | grep "route=chat-" | awk '{print $NF}' | sort | uniq -c
- jq shorthand to extract sequence_length from JSON logs: jq '.request.sequence_length'
- small script to compute tokens/min from log window: python -c "import sys,json; ..."  # placeholder

Open questions / unresolved:
- Why did batching window increase automatically yesterday? Was there a rollout? Check flag-change history (flags-api)
- Are there any long-lived KV-cache evictions tied to model upgrades last week? Check runtimes/upgrade/2026-02-28 notes

End-of-shift handoff notes (if I need to bail):
- If spike persists, lock the "se-sandbox" route to 10qps and reroute to dedicated low-cost pool (gpool-scratch)
- Leave final metrics paste in #infra-ops with timestamp and short list of actions taken

One-liners to paste in Slack when done:
- "Morning queue check: tokens/min 1.2M -> took batching + kv-cache actions, watching for 30m. If still up, will canary model variant q4_0 for heavy routes."
- "Scaling watch: spare GPUs 1 -> filed scale request if projected burst > 10%"

Random personal reminder:
- Follow up with platform-team retro: bring a short note about "automatic batching drift" for next Tuesday sync.

---
End of scratchpad. Will convert high-priority todos to INFRA tickets after verifying with Aisha.
